text: I think constant smartphone connection harms deep focus more than it helps. Many people say the phone is useful because we can search information fast, and this is true in some part. But for the deep and long focus, the always-on notification is a big problem. Every small buzz pull your attention away, and after that you need long time to come back to the real task. Last semester I have a strong example from my own life. I was writing a research report at night, and I put my phone beside my laptop because I think maybe my group will message me. In two hours my phone vibrate so many times, from group chat, from one app about a sale, from a friend who send a video. Each time I tell myself only one quick look, but one look became ten minutes of scrolling. When I finally finish, the report which should take two hours took almost the whole night, and the quality was not so good because my thinking was always cutted into small pieces. So from this experience I learned that the connectivity itself is not bad, the problem is when it is constant and we cannot control it. Now I keep my phone in other room when I study, and my focus become much more deep and calm. This small change show me that we should use the technology, but not let the technology use our attention all the time.
